WITH order_invoice_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    o.order_id,
    COUNT(i.invoice_number) as invoice_count
  FROM Orders o
  LEFT JOIN Invoices i ON o.order_id = i.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id
),
total_invoices AS (
  SELECT SUM(invoice_count) as total_count
  FROM order_invoice_counts
),
order_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    oic.order_id,
    oic.invoice_count,
    CAST(oic.invoice_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / NULLIF(ti.total_count, 0) as share
  FROM order_invoice_counts oic
  CROSS JOIN total_invoices ti
),
average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM order_shares
),
above_average_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    os.invoice_count,
    os.share,
    ashr.avg_share
  FROM order_shares os
  CROSS JOIN average_share ashr
  WHERE os.share > ashr.avg_share
)
SELECT 
  SUM(invoice_count) as total_invoices,
  AVG(share) as average_share,
  AVG(share - avg_share) as average_excess
FROM above_average_orders

assumptions.assumption: If the total invoice count is zero, all shares become NULL via NULLIF, no orders exceed a NULL average, and the result is an empty set. The request does not specify this edge case.
